evidence: Prisc. p. 939 P.: prōnōmen, as sibi, sē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Priscian’s prōnōmen reciprocum, the pronoun that “turns back” on the subject: sē, sibi (Traupman 224). Classically the adjective means going back and forth, ebbing (Pliny).

phrases.latin: Dā exempla prōnōminis reciprocī. — Sē, sibi.
phrases.english: Give some examples of a reflexive pronoun. — Himself, to himself.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 224.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
